# Security Hunter Ledger

One line per entry, newest last.

- 2026-09-23 | FIXED | gateway-http | `Connectors.Calendar.calendar_query/2` and `calendar_delete/3` folded an agent-supplied `calendar` name straight into a filesystem path (`{workspace_agent_dir}/events/{calendar}/...`) with no validation, unlike the sibling `Email.validate_folder_name/1`; a `../`-laden `calendar` from the CalendarQuery/CalendarDelete tool call lets an agent read (and, via the follow-on CalDAV delete, remove) a cached-event JSON file anywhere the gateway process can reach, outside its own workspace tree | lib/tri_onyx/connectors/calendar.ex
- 2026-09-23 | DOWNGRADED | gateway-http | `caldav_report/4`, `caldav_put/4`, and `caldav_delete/3` fold their `path`/`href` argument unescaped into the raw CalDAV request line built in `caldav_request/5` (`"#{method} #{path} HTTP/1.1\r\n..."`) — an embedded CRLF there would splice extra headers or a second request onto the credentialed connection to the CalDAV server (classic HTTP request/header injection). Today's fix closes this for `calendar_query/2`'s `calendar` (now validated before it reaches `caldav_report/4`), but `calendar_create/1` still passes `draft["calendar"]` into the same `href` construction unchecked, and `calendar_update/1`'s `draft["href"]`/`draft["etag"]` are fully agent-controlled and reach `caldav_put/4`/the request line with no validation at all. None of this is provable without a live or mocked CalDAV endpoint to observe the smuggled request/response, which this environment (no Docker, no network) can't drive end-to-end — worth a human's review | lib/tri_onyx/connectors/calendar.ex
- 2026-09-23 | NO-FINDING | gateway-http | Reviewed router.ex end to end against the four already-open PRs from prior runs (#35 images traversal, #41 connector_handler timing compare, #46 webhook X-Forwarded-For, #51 rate-limiter window race) plus their own NO-FINDING sweep of webhook_signature.ex/webhook_rate_limiter.ex/system_command.ex/bcp/validator.ex — nothing new found in those files. `/api/workspace/file`, `/pages/:commit/*page_path`, and `Workspace.resolve_canonical/1` → `RepoStore.read_file_at_commit/log/changed_paths` reviewed: commit SHAs are regex-validated, `git show sha:path` can't traverse via `..` (not a real path in git's tree object model), and `--` before pathspecs in `RepoStore.log/2` blocks option injection from the `path` query param. Management endpoints (`/bcp/approvals`, `/webhook-endpoints`, `/agents/*`, etc.) have no bearer auth, but `docs/webhook-receiver-design.md` documents this as intentional — only `/hooks/:endpoint_id` is exposed through the Cloudflare Tunnel, everything else is local-only port 4000 — so absence of auth there isn't a new finding. Also considered and killed: the `String.starts_with?(host_path, expanded_agent_dir)` (no trailing separator) checks in `agent_session.ex`'s send_email/save_draft/calendar_create/calendar_update handlers look like the same bug class as the fixed `/images` route, but `Workspace.agent_dir/1` always ends in the fixed literal segment `/self`, which makes a same-class sibling-prefix collision unreachable (proved by writing a failing test first — it passed on unpatched code too, so no PR filed for it) | lib/tri_onyx/router.ex, lib/tri_onyx/agent_session.ex
